transcript:
Header:
Date/Time: 2026-12-29 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Arjun Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (OrionCloud Head of Partnerships), Samir Desai (OrionCloud Cloud Integrations Lead), Priya Rao (OrionCloud Solution Architect)
Shared artifacts: Redwood marketplace checklist (link: https://tinyurl.com/redwood-marketplace-checklist), initial reference arch sketch (shared in chat), OrionCloud partner brief (link: https://orioncloud.com/partners/brief)

Summary:
Quick technical sync to cover what Orion needs to get listed in the OrionCloud marketplace with an integrated Redwood runtime offering (joint solution). Focus on listing metadata/billing, reference architecture options (hosted vs private, VPC peering), security/compliance, and next steps for the engineering teams.

Topics covered: marketplace listing reqs; billing & metering; reference arch options; private deployment/VPC; security (SOC2/SSO/KMS); timeline and owners.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call — Maya from Redwood, Arjun our SE, and from OrionCloud?
[00:07] Lena Ortiz: Hi uh Lena here, Samir and Priya also on. Thanks for setting this up.
[00:12] Arjun Patel: Hey all, Arjun. I'll be driving the reference architecture side.
[00:15] Samir Desai: Samir. We wanted to see what the marketplace listing looks like and how billing would work with usage metering.
[00:22] Maya Chen: Yep, perfect. High level agenda: marketplace onboarding checklist, billing/metering, two reference arch options (hosted Redwood in Redwood Dedicated vs Orion-managed private deployment with VPC peering), and security/compliance callouts.
[00:34] Priya Rao: Quick note — we have a procurement window in mid-Feb, so timeline is kinda tight.
[00:38] Maya Chen: Good to know. We'll try to keep action items tight.

[02:10] Arjun Patel: So, starting with marketplace listing requirements — from Redwood side we need: product metadata (title, description), supported models/versions, pricing model, support SLAs, dev contacts, and a short reference architecture blurb. We have a sample listing in the doc I just posted. (link: tinyurl)
[02:28] Samir Desai: For billing, can Redwood surface metered usage to OrionCloud so you can bill end customers through our marketplace? Or do we need to route billing via Redwood and we invoice Orion?
[02:40] Maya Chen: Two options — marketplace reseller flow where Redwood invoices Orion for consumed tokens (we provide metering exports + invoice), or a direct marketplace metering integration where we push usage into your marketplace metering API. We support both but the direct integration requires API keys and some mapping work.
[02:59] Samir Desai: Do you have an API spec for metering?
[03:03] Arjun Patel: Yes, we have a metering API — it's webhook + push endpoint. I'll attach the spec after the call. It includes per-request token counts and model variant labels. We sometimes mis-transcribe model names in the export so watch out, but the payload is stable.

[05:22] Priya Rao: On the reference arch — we sketched two paths, right? Redwood-hosted (Redwood Dedicated behind a marketplace listing) and Orion-hosted (private deployment with Redwood runtime deployed in our VPC). Pros/cons?
[05:33] Arjun Patel: Exactly. Redwood-hosted: fastest time to market, Redwood manages infra and scaling, Redwood provides SLA and observability. Billing can be straightforward since usage is centralized. Downside: data residency and some enterprise customers prefer VPC.
[05:49] Arjun Patel: Orion-hosted/private: gives you full data control, can satisfy regulated customers, but requires more ops work — we provide a private control plane and an on-prem package; we'll need VPC peering, IAM service accounts, and KMS integration. Latency is often lower to your other services.
[06:05] Samir Desai: For VPC peering, do you support cross-account peering or only a managed connector?
[06:10] Arjun Patel: We support both. We can do classic VPC peering, or an SSM/connector model if peering is restricted. We'll need IP ranges, and we recommend private endpoints to keep traffic internal. Priya, can you share your VPC constraints?
[06:23] Priya Rao: Yes, I'll send our network ranges and the terraform snippet. We use centralized egress via Transit Gateway so peering pattern might need a small adjustment.

[08:16] Lena Ortiz: On the marketplace listing itself, what's the approvals flow? Do we need Redwood legal to sign a marketplace master agreement?
[08:24] Maya Chen: Typically yes. For marketplace listings we have a partner agreement + listing terms. For reseller billing we have an MSA addendum. I'll loop in our legal. Lena, can you share Orion's standard partner agreement template so we can compare?
[08:38] Lena Ortiz: Yep will share.

[10:02] Samir Desai: Security/compliance — customers ask for SOC2, SSO integration, and audit logs. Does Redwood provide these?
[10:10] Maya Chen: Yes: SOC2 Type II, SSO via SAML/OIDC (we support SAML 2.0), RBAC, audit logs, and KMS integrations for customer-managed keys. We also capture request-level logs for a configurable retention window; longer retention is an add-on.
[10:27] Samir Desai: For KMS, do you support AWS KMS and HSM?
[10:32] Arjun Patel: We support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and can integrate with customer HSM via an on-prem key proxy. There's some setup for private deployments to ensure keys never leave customer control.

[12:45] Priya Rao: One thing — performance. For the joint solution, some of our customers want predictable latency under 500ms for short prompts. How do you handle that?
[12:54] Arjun Patel: We have Dedicated pools you can reserve. For example, we can pin model variants and provide autoscaling policies to hit a p95 latency SLO. Also batching and KV cache behavior affects token-level latency; we'll include suggested batch sizes and quantization profiles in the ref arch doc.
[13:15] Priya Rao: Great. Any benchmark artifacts we can run in our environment?
[13:19] Maya Chen: We can run a short POC benchmark — Arjun can provide a small harness and sample prompts. It needs access to a test endpoint or your VPC if doing private.

[16:40] Arjun Patel: Back to listing metadata — pricing model options: flat per-invocation, per-token, or tiered reserved capacity. Marketplace often wants a SKU and unit. We recommend per-token with a list price and a marketplace discount code for Orion.
[16:58] Samir Desai: For metering granularity, do you report per-request token counts or aggregated daily totals?
[17:03] Arjun Patel: We can do both; best practice is per-request events so your billing system can re-aggregate if needed. We'll include request id and model variant. Note: sometimes transcription exports show model labels like "redwood-v2-lite" as "redwood v two lite" — small mismatch in old exports, fixed in new schema.

[20:12] Lena Ortiz: Contracting — how do we handle revenue share? Will Redwood report gross usage and invoice Orion monthly?
[20:20] Maya Chen: Two patterns we've seen: reseller model (Redwood invoices Orion for gross usage and Orion bills end customers) or pass-through model where Marketplace captures usage and pays Redwood directly and we credit Orion. We'll need legal to pick.

[23:05] Priya Rao: Integration work level — roughly how much engineering effort to enable VPC private deployment and metering hooking?
[23:12] Arjun Patel: For a standard private deployment with VPC peering and KMS, estimate 2-3 weeks of joint engineering work if both sides allocate one engineer part-time. Metering direct integration ~1 week to wire endpoints and test. Docs and checklist speed this up.
[23:30] Samir Desai: Okay that fits our Feb procurement window if we start early Jan.

[27:45] Arjun Patel: I'll outline the reference architecture choices in the diagram: 
- Option A: Redwood-hosted marketplace listing -> Redwood Dedicated pools -> Redwood exposes endpoint -> Orion marketplace forwards to Redwood; billing via reseller or API push.
- Option B: Orion-hosted private runtime -> Redwood private control plane + runtime deployed in Orion VPC -> VPC peering / private endpoints -> billing via Orion metering capture.
(Arjun shared a quick sketch in the chat)

[31:02] Maya Chen: A few practical items: 1) we'll need a sandbox account/credentials for the POC; 2) marketplace listing assets (logos, descriptions) — Lena will collate; 3) legal templates and billing model decision.
[31:18] Lena Ortiz: I'll collect marketing assets and share by next week.
[31:22] Priya Rao: I'll send VPC ranges and sample terraform by EOD Monday.

[35:40] Samir Desai: Any concerns around data exfil? Some regulated customers require no logs leave the VPC.
[35:48] Arjun Patel: For private deployments we can ensure request logs and KV cache stay inside the customer's VPC. For hosted offering we can encrypt-in-transit and at-rest and offer customer-managed KMS for key control; but some customers still require total on-prem. We'll document this clearly in the ref arch doc.

[39:05] Maya Chen: Competitors we sometimes see on Orion side are CloudMart and AuroraCloud; but our differentiator is the production-first runtime and direct support for dedicated and private modes.
[39:20] Lena Ortiz: Noted. Procurement teams will ask comparisons.

[42:10] Arjun Patel: I'll also include suggested autoscale policies and example config for reserved capacity and burst targets in the ref arch doc so your SREs can review.

[45:00] Maya Chen: Ok let's recap next steps and owners. Arjun, you'll draft the reference architecture diagram and include metering API spec and autoscale suggestions. Maya will share marketplace onboarding checklist and loop legal. Priya to send VPC details and terraform snippet. Lena to gather marketplace assets and run legal template.
[45:22] Lena Ortiz: Sounds good.
[45:30] Priya Rao: We'll try to get our terraform and network ranges by Monday.

[46:10] Maya Chen: Awesome. I'll send a follow-up email with the links and calendar invites for a POC kickoff the week of Jan 4th provisional.
[46:20] Samir Desai: Thanks everyone.
[46:25] Arjun Patel: Thanks, talk soon.
[46:28] Meeting end.

Notes about transcription: occasional mis-attrubutions and small transcription artifacts — e.g., "KV cache" sometimes appeared as "KV cash" in earlier exports; model labels might be spelled out in speech.

Recap / Next steps (copied):
- Maya to share marketplace onboarding checklist and sample listing (link + doc) by 2027-01-03.
- Arjun to draft reference architecture diagram, include metering API spec and autoscale recommendations, upload by 2027-01-07.
- Priya to provide VPC ranges and example terraform by 2027-01-05.
- Lena to coordinate legal and marketplace assets, confirm billing model by 2027-01-10.

Action items (simple list):
- Maya Chen: share onboarding checklist & legal contact (due 2027-01-03)
- Arjun Patel: ref-arch diagram + metering spec (due 2027-01-07)
- Priya Rao: VPC ranges + terraform snippet (due 2027-01-05)

End of transcript.
